images.title: Olaudah Equiano, or Gustavus Vassa, the African
images.object_date: Original engraving published 1 March 1789; digital reproduction in Project Gutenberg edition
images.maker: Daniel Orme, after W. Denton; original published by Olaudah Equiano (Gustavus Vassa)
images.rights: Public domain in the USA; faithful reproduction of a historical engraving. Project Gutenberg ebook 15399 is designated public domain.
images.credit: Project Gutenberg; engraving by Daniel Orme after W. Denton
images.caption: Equiano’s frontispiece portrait. The original engraving was published on 1 March 1789. The caption displays both Olaudah Equiano and Gustavus Vassa.
images.alt: Engraved portrait of Equiano wearing a coat and neckcloth, holding an open book and looking at the viewer. Both names appear beneath the portrait.
images.display_note: Use at approximately 300–400px wide; source is 455px wide. The book is visible, but its text cannot be read confidently in this reproduction.

images.title: Anti-Slavery Cameo
images.object_type: Photograph of a jasperware medallion in a gold mount
images.object_date: Medallion 1787; early nineteenth-century gold mounting according to the Commons/Walters record
images.maker: William Hackwood (designer); Josiah Wedgwood and Sons (manufacturer)
images.rights: Photograph CC BY-SA 3.0 via Wikimedia Commons; artwork public domain. The current Walters object page also links CC0, but this distribution retains the Commons photograph attribution/license.
images.credit: Walters Art Museum, museum purchase 1989, 48.2597; photograph via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0
images.caption: Wedgwood antislavery medallion, 1787, in a later gold mount. An unnamed chained figure kneels with raised hands. Walters Art Museum, 48.2597.
images.alt: Black-and-white photograph of a ceramic cameo in a decorative gold mount. A chained man kneels, with his hands together and raised before his face.
images.display_note: The kneeling figure and chains are clear. Do not claim students can read the motto in this photograph: the inscription is recorded by the museum but is not legible here.

images.title: Diagram of Ship Transporting Enslaved People
images.object_type: Photographic reproduction of a foldout engraving
images.maker: Published in Thomas Clarkson’s history of the abolition of the African slave trade; plate signed Hensley sculp.
images.provenance: University of Virginia Special Collections, as credited by Encyclopedia Virginia
images.rights: Underlying 1808 engraving is public domain. This is a faithful reproduction of that two-dimensional work; no express reuse license was stated on the image record.
images.credit: University of Virginia Special Collections, via Encyclopedia Virginia
images.caption: Brookes ship diagram, published in Thomas Clarkson’s 1808 history of abolition. It represents another vessel, decades after the crossing narrated by Equiano; it is not a reconstruction of his ship.
images.alt: An 1808 engraving with a side section, deck plans and cross sections of the slave ship Brookes, showing rows of tightly arranged human figures.
images.display_note: Offer an open-full-image link. Distinguish this 1808 plate from the earlier 1788–89 diagram tradition. Do not assign a total passenger count without analysis of this exact version.

selection_notes: No Getty-watermarked supplied portrait was republished.
